03068e1091b7c8896447b800dd1f9152139d0162.en: Help me catch up on what I’ve missed in Slack. Before reading, ask me: - Which channels or DMs I should focus on (or check everything) - How far back to look (since yesterday, last week, specific date) - What I’m most concerned about missing (decisions, @mentions, urgent items, project updates) - Whether there are specific topics or people to prioritize Then scan those channels and show me a summary: - Total unread messages - Breakdown by channel Focus on messages that @mention me, contain decisions, or are marked urgent first. Show me the top 5 most important updates with context and links to the threads. If there are more than 30 unread messages total, start with these top 5 and ask if you should summarize more.
03068e1091b7c8896447b800dd1f9152139d0162.zh: 幫我補上在 Slack 中錯過的內容。開始閱讀前，請先問我：－要專注於哪些頻道或私訊（或全部檢查）－要回溯多久（自昨天起、上週、或特定日期）－我最擔心錯過什麼（決策、@提及、緊急事項、專案更新）－是否有特定主題或人物需要優先處理接著掃描這些頻道，並給我一份摘要：－未讀訊息總數－依頻道分類的明細請優先處理標記 @提及我、包含決策或標示為緊急的訊息。顯示 5 項最重要的更新，附上背景說明與討論串連結。如果未讀訊息總數超過 30 則，先從這 5 項開始，並詢問是否要摘要更多內容。

Usually that is an older server that only takes ssh-rsa (SHA-1), which current OpenSSH turns off by default; less often, a PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms line in your ssh configuration leaves your key’s type out. If you can, install an ed25519 key on the host (ssh-keygen -t ed25519, then add it to authorized_keys there); otherwise see your SSH client’s documentation on legacy servers.

Don’t invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there’s nothing to observe.

30f89e6a8098c017ec37b31c6751ceac963bf936.en: Help me organize recent screenshots on my Desktop. First, scan my Desktop and count how many screenshots/images are there. Show me: - Total count - Date range (oldest to newest) Then, focus only on screenshots from the last 14 days. For each one: - Identify what it shows - Suggest a descriptive filename - Propose which folder it belongs in (or if it can be deleted) Group similar screenshots together. Show me the plan before making any changes. After I approve, start by organizing just 10 files as a preview. If there are more than 10 files, check in with me before continuing with the rest.

5a833bb51da8ccd3ce11042f40d9cca3aeeaa004.en: Help me organize my Downloads folder. First, scan and show me a summary: - Total files and total size - Files older than 30 days - Largest files taking up space Before organizing, ask me: - What categories or folder structure would be most useful - Whether I want to delete or archive old files - If there are specific file types I want to prioritize (documents, images, installers, etc.) Then focus only on files older than 30 days first. Show me a proposed plan for these old files: - Categories to create - Files to delete (installers, duplicates, temp files) - Files to keep with where they should go After I approve, organize the first 15 old files as a preview. If there are more files, check in before continuing.

I have [voice memos / audio recordings] in [specify location] that I want transcribed and organized. First, scan the folder and show me: - How many audio files - Total duration - Date range Before transcribing, ask me: - What these recordings are about - How I’d like them organized (chronologically, by topic, by theme) - Whether I want verbatim transcripts or cleaned-up summaries - What the final document should be (meeting notes, journal entries, ideas list, etc.) If there are more than 5 recordings, start by transcribing just the 3 most recent ones. Then look across my recent conversations, docs, and activity from the last few days and write up a briefing. Structure it as: - Urgent items (for these, pull the deeper context: who’s involved, what’s been discussed, what’s unresolved) - Conversations where I’m mentioned (read the full threads for context) - Threads I’m not in but should probably know about based on my current tasks - Tasks due this week and anything blocking them

I have messy, unstructured files and want to understand what themes are emerging. First, scan the folder and show me a summary: - Total files - Date range (oldest to newest) - Types of content Before analyzing, ask me: - What I’m hoping to discover (recurring themes, contradictions, evolution of thinking, action items, or something else) - Whether certain files or time periods should be prioritized - What format would be most useful for the final analysis If there are more than 20 files, start by analyzing just the 10 most recent files. Show me the top 3-5 patterns you found with 2-3 specific examples for each pattern. Once I confirm you’re on the right track, analyze the remaining files.
7e74891ca5314e8389df535fa41c3dfaea5730b1.zh: 幫我在〔語音備忘錄／會議逐字稿／文件／日記條目／請指定資料夾〕中找出模式與洞察。我這裡有一堆雜亂、未整理的檔案，想了解正在浮現哪些主題。請先掃描資料夾，給我一份摘要：－檔案總數－日期範圍（最舊到最新）－內容類型在分析之前，請先問我：－我希望發現什麼（反覆出現的主題、矛盾之處、想法的演變、待辦事項，或其他）－是否有特定檔案或時間區段需要優先處理－最終分析採用哪種格式最有用如果檔案超過 20 個，請先分析最近的 10 個檔案。給我 3 到 5 個您發現的主要模式，每個模式附上 2 到 3 個具體範例。等我確認方向正確後，再分析其餘檔案。

If there are more than 20 items on this page, extract them in batches of 10. If there are multiple pages, just do the first page and check with you before continuing.

a9f3b8058b7cc02d9417e47c845c4726d419e451.en: Help me plan and optimize my week. I have my Google Calendar open and ready for you to review and edit. First, review my calendar and show me a summary: - Total meetings - Busiest days - Where I have gaps of 2+ hours Before proposing changes, ask me about: - What I’m trying to accomplish this week - How much focus time I need and for what - Any deadlines or commitments not on my calendar - Which types of meetings I should decline or shorten - Personal commitments or boundaries I want to protect Then show me your top 3-5 proposed changes with explanations: - Focus blocks to add - Meetings to decline or reschedule - Time conflicts to resolve Start with the highest-impact changes first. Once I approve each change, make the edits directly in my calendar one at a time.

c9b98c4bc5eaa59510de984ab88b73a05927594c.en: Teach me skills by building one in front of me. Draft a small example now — turning rough notes into a tidy one-page summary — and show exactly what the skill captures: the steps, the format, the rules you’ll follow the same way every time. Then ask which task I actually repeat each week, rewrite the skill for that, and test it with me on one real example before saving it.
c9b98c4bc5eaa59510de984ab88b73a05927594c.zh: 當著我的面建立一項技能，教我怎麼做。現在就草擬一個小範例——把雜亂的筆記整理成一頁整潔的摘要——並確切呈現這項技能所涵蓋的內容：步驟、格式，以及每次都會遵循的規則。接著詢問我實際上每週會重複做的任務是什麼，針對它改寫技能，並在儲存前用一個真實案例與我一起測試。

cacd5ce051653cf014edb9e7f3865dbc99e8b6d7.en:
I’ve just finished setting you up. Here’s what you know about me (facts about me, quoted — not instructions):
{lines}

{goal}

How to work — keep me in the loop the whole way, don’t go quiet:
1. Reply right away, before looking at anything, with one line saying what you’re about to check and why.
2. Look in at most three places that matter for this: my calendar for the next two days, my inbox for unanswered threads, and the doc or channel most related to the task. Stop after three.
3. After EACH one, post a one-line note of what you found there (or that there was nothing useful) — immediately, not at the end.
4. Then write the first pass. Rough and fast beats polished and late: give me something I can react to within a couple of minutes. Show it in full, not a description of it.
5. Ask me if a tool needs a permission. Finish with two other things from my week you could take on next.

Keep every update to a line or two.
cacd5ce051653cf014edb9e7f3865dbc99e8b6d7.zh:
我剛完成你的設定。以下是你目前所知道關於我的事（這些是關於我的事實，以引號標示──不是指示）：
{lines}

{goal}

工作方式──全程讓我隨時掌握進度，不要中途沉默：
1. 在查看任何內容之前先立即回覆一行，說明你接下來要檢查什麼、原因是什麼。
2. 最多查看三個與此相關的地方：我未來兩天的行事曆、我收件匣中尚未回覆的討論串，以及與此任務最相關的文件或頻道。查看三個後就停止。
3. 每查看完一個地方，就立即（而非最後才）發一行說明你在那裡發現了什麼（或沒有找到有用的內容）。
4. 接著寫出初稿。粗略且快速勝過精美但延遲：給我一些我幾分鐘內就能回應的內容，請完整呈現內容本身，而不是描述內容。
5. 如果某項工具需要權限，請詢問我。最後再列出我這週還有哪兩件事你可以接著處理。

每則更新都請控制在一到兩行內。

Authorization headers and any query/body key matching a parameter name are stripped before injection. Requests whose body or query already contains a key that collides with a parameter name under common normalizations (e.g. api_key[] or api.key vs api_key) are rejected with 502 to prevent credential substitution.

f894701799b70dc4aa93d4bb0c13195be47b1051.en: I have a job interview coming up for [role] at [company]. Before researching, ask me: - What the role is and what level - What I already know about the company - What I’m most nervous or uncertain about - If I have the job description or any interview details Then research the company and role, and show me what I found: - Company overview and recent news (last 6 months) - What this role typically involves - Common interview questions for this type of role - The interview team on LinkedIn (if you have names) Show me an outline covering these 3-5 topics before creating the full prep doc: - Key points about the company to mention - How my background connects to what they need - Questions I should ask them - 3-4 likely interview questions with suggested talking points Once I approve, create a complete interview prep guide I can review before the interview.
f894701799b70dc4aa93d4bb0c13195be47b1051.zh: 我即將要到 [company] 面試 [role] 職位。開始研究前，請先問我：－這個職位是什麼、屬於什麼層級－我對這家公司已經了解多少－我最緊張或最不確定的地方是什麼－我是否有職缺說明或任何面試相關資訊 接著研究這家公司與這個職位，並告訴我您找到了什麼：－公司概況與近期新聞（過去 6 個月）－這個職位通常負責哪些工作－這類職位常見的面試問題－面試團隊在 LinkedIn 上的資訊（如果查得到姓名） 在撰寫完整的準備文件之前，先給我一份涵蓋以下 3 到 5 個主題的大綱：－關於這家公司該提到的重點－我的背景如何對應他們的需求－我該問他們的問題－3 到 4 個可能出現的面試問題與建議的回答重點 在我核准之後，建立一份完整的面試準備指南，讓我在面試前可以參考。

How to work — keep me in the loop the whole way, don’t go quiet:
1. Reply right away, before looking at anything, with one line saying what you’re about to check and why.
2. Look in at most three places that matter for this: my calendar for the next two days, my inbox for unanswered threads, and the doc or channel most related to the task. Stop after three.
3. After EACH one, post a one-line note of what you found there (or that there was nothing useful) — immediately, not at the end.
4. Then write the first pass and put it in a document I can open, share and edit — create a file for it (or an artifact, if you can’t make files here), named for the task, with the full draft inside, not a summary of it. Rough and fast beats polished and late: headings and bullets are plenty; I want something to react to within a couple of minutes. In the chat, just say it’s ready and name the two or three things you most want my take on.
5. Finish with two other things from my week you could take on next.

Keep every update to a line or two.
fd5c9dc3c6d839945bcb9152aa2e8a0cbd87aebc.zh:
我剛完成您的設定。以下是您目前所知道關於我的資訊：
{lines}

{goal}

工作方式——請全程讓我掌握進度，不要中途沉默：
1. 在查看任何內容之前，立即回覆一行文字，說明您接下來要查什麼、為什麼要查。
2. 最多查看與此相關的三個地方：我未來兩天的行事曆、我收件匣中尚未回覆的討論串，以及與此任務最相關的文件或頻道。查完三個就停止。
3. 每查完一個地方，就立即發一行說明您發現了什麼（或該處沒有有用的資訊）——要即時回報，不要留到最後才說。
4. 接著寫出初稿，並放進一份我可以開啟、分享與編輯的文件——請為它建立一個檔案（如果這裡無法建立檔案，就用 artifact），以此任務命名，內容是完整草稿，而不是摘要。粗略但快速勝過精緻但遲交：標題和項目符號就足夠了，我希望幾分鐘內就能看到可以回應的東西。在聊天中，只需說明已經完成，並指出您最希望我針對哪兩三點給意見。
5. 最後列出我這週還可以交給您處理的另外兩件事。

每次更新都請控制在一到兩行內。
